long_biography.plain_text:
Shipyards gave Jonsson his first view of capital-intensive, cyclical business. After studying at Gothenburg, he worked on the proposed combination of Götaverken and Eriksberg, then moved through shipbuilding sales, petroleum transport and leadership of a worldwide marine-services company. That industrial background preceded his 1986 move to the United States.

In Seattle, Jonsson began with downtown property investments and an apartment development near Microsoft's emerging campus before forming the group he still chairs. Its interests expanded across the United States, Sweden and Spain, with day-to-day leadership later passing to the next generation. Public service ran alongside investment: he represented Sweden as an honorary consul and helped establish university exchange and children's-health initiatives.
